structural_development.rationale: The PRE response is a terse two-descriptor list. The POST response elaborates the brand's core values into five named values, each accompanied by an explanatory clause (e.g., 'Helping users both fall asleep faster and wake up naturally'). This is a substantial expansion in the number of values, scope, and explanatory depth — multiple new clauses and explanatory passages added.

semantic_events.post_evidence: User-Centric Design – Focused on real-world needs, ensuring effortless use and convenience.
semantic_events.rationale: Both concepts occupy the user-focused / customer-oriented semantic neighborhood, but the organizing frame shifts: PRE frames the value as audience-orientation (centering the customer), while POST frames it as a design/operational principle (user-centric design centered on real-world needs and effortless use). The subsumption test fails ('User-Centric Design is a specific way of being customer-centricity' is not clearly true; user-centric design is a sibling operationalization rather than a strict subtype), so Reframed is the correct tier-2 verdict.

After mandatory recheck against all five POST concepts, no defensible transformation holds. Nearest counterpart User-Centric Design sits in a different conceptual domain (audience-orientation vs attribute-standard). Quality remains absent from the POST response.
